question: The first five-year plan of India was based on which model?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Harrod-Domar Model**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first five-year plan of India was based on the **Harrod-Domar Model**.
 
• The **Harrod-Domar Model** is a classical economic theory which suggests that the growth rate of an economy is directly related to the level of savings and the productivity of investment.
 
• This model was chosen as it emphasized the importance of investment and savings to spur economic growth, which was crucial for India's development post-independence.
 
• The first five-year plan, spanning from 1951 to 1956, focused on the agricultural sector, aiming to increase food production and address the food shortages of the time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Five-Year Plans** were central to India's planned economic development strategy, with the Planning Commission playing a key role in formulating and overseeing their implementation.
 
• The **Planning Commission** was established in 1950 and was responsible for assessing the country's resources, formulating plans for their most effective and balanced utilization, and determining priorities.
 
• The success of the first five-year plan set the foundation for subsequent plans, which continued to shape India's economic policies and strategies for decades.
 
• Over time, the focus of the five-year plans shifted from agriculture to industrialization, infrastructure development, and later, to social sectors such as education and health.
 
• In 2015, the Planning Commission was replaced by the **NITI Aayog**, which now serves as the policy think-tank of the Government of India, providing strategic and technical advice on key policy matters.
